clue.text: Drivers should avoid it, and what passes through it

definitions.meaning: a narrow stretch of road where traffic jams build up
the slender top of a wine bottle, through which the drink pours

explanation.surface: Motorists keep away from a hold-up, and wine is poured through it.
explanation.definitionFit: A traffic choke point is called this, and it is literally the narrow throat of a flask through which liquid flows.

clue.text: I rose to receive the king a terrible person

indicators.note: to receive means the reversed piece takes another letter inside it
in a down clue, rising means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: ego is Latin for I, the self
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Someone stood up to welcome the monarch, who turned out to be a brute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rose' turns EGO into OGE in this down entry; 'to receive' puts R inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A fairy-tale giant who eats people, used loosely of any cruel, frightening individual.

clue.text: I want a new name for Formosa

indicators.note: new tells us the three words are made into a fresh arrangement of letters

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a fresh name for the island once called Formosa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' signals an anagram of I WANT A.
explanation.definitionFit: Formosa was the Portuguese-derived former name of the East Asian island now known by this name.

clue.text: How time flies!

parts.note: the exclamation describes the way hours pass by, slipping away one after another

explanation.definitionFit: The verb describes time passing or running out, which is what the exclamation marvels at.

clue.text: Prepare to put out with the rising tide

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the word tide is read upwards, from its last letter to its first

explanation.surface: Get ready to launch the boat as the water comes in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prepare to put out' sounds nautical but means get text ready for publication.
explanation.definitionFit: To ready a text for publication is to correct and revise it before release.

clue.text: The skin doctor comes from S.E. England

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dermatologist hails from the south-east of England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' looks like a noun after 'skin' but is the anagram signal on THE SKIN. KENT is a county in south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes someone or something native to Kent, a county in the south-east corner of the country.

clue.text: From France a choice prune

parts.note: something from France is French
a plum is a choice thing, the pick of the bunch, as in a plum job

explanation.surface: A top-quality dried fruit imported from France.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a variety of dried fruit, Agen prunes, made from a plum grown in south-west France.

clue.text: Pipe bursts each summer

indicators.note: bursts suggests the words are broken apart and the letters scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A water pipe bursts every summer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pipe' suggests plumbing; it is a tobacco pipe. 'bursts' signals an anagram of EACH SUMMER.
explanation.definitionFit: A tobacco pipe with a bowl carved from a soft white clay mineral.

clue.text: The charge is about right but you don't have to pay

indicators.note: is about means the charge goes around the other letter

parts.note: a fee is a charge for a service

explanation.surface: The fee seems fair, but in fact no payment is needed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is about' puts R inside FEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something costing nothing, gratis, is something one need not spend money on.

clue.text: Noise interrupts speech in church ceremony

indicators.note: interrupts means the noise breaks into the middle of the speech

parts.note: an oration is a formal speech
din is a loud noise

explanation.surface: A racket breaks out during a sermon at a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Noise' looks like the subject of the sentence; 'interrupts' makes it break into the middle of the speech.
explanation.definitionFit: The rite in which a person is made a priest or minister is a formal service of the church.

clue.text: A hewer of wood and a drawer of water

definitions.meaning: a craftsman who shapes wood on a lathe
a painter, J.M.W. ..., famous for seascapes and stormy water scenes

explanation.surface: The biblical phrase for menial labourers who chop logs and fetch from the well.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue borrows the Bible's 'hewers of wood and drawers of water' (menial labourers), but a drawer here is an artist.
explanation.definitionFit: A lathe worker shapes timber, and the great English artist painted the sea.

clue.text: Let bank arrange cover for retirement

indicators.note: arrange tells us to put the letters of the two words into a different order

explanation.surface: Allow a bank to set up insurance for someone's pension.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retirement' suggests a pension, but it means going to bed. 'arrange' signals an anagram of LET BANK.
explanation.definitionFit: A woollen bed covering is what one pulls over oneself on retiring for the night.

clue.text: Certainly using every available method

definitions.meaning: a polite way of saying of course, yes
literally, through all possible ways of doing something

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a courteous assent, and read literally it means with all the resources one has.

clue.text: Relation gets can in summer

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Relation gets can in summer' for ACCOUNTANT: ACCOUNT (relation) + ANT fits, but nothing in 'can in' gives ANT, so the clue looks misread or cut short; no source found.

clue.text: It has been turned into a Massenet opera

indicators.note: been turned into says the two words are changed into something else by rearranging their letters

explanation.surface: Some story has been adapted as an opera by Massenet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has been turned into' reads as adaptation; 'been turned into' signals an anagram of IT HAS.
explanation.definitionFit: This 1894 opera by the French composer Jules Massenet tells of an Egyptian courtesan.

clue.text: Possibly spy on fashionable medium

indicators.note: possibly suggests one might rearrange the letters of the next word

parts.note: chic means stylish or fashionable

explanation.surface: Perhaps a stylish spiritualist is a secret agent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' turns SPY into PSY.
explanation.definitionFit: A medium is a person who claims to contact the dead, a clairvoyant with supposed paranormal powers.

clue.text: Song performed by little Sarah in the afternoon

indicators.note: in means the short name sits inside the afternoon abbreviation

parts.note: PM, post meridiem, means after noon
Sal is a pet form of the name Sarah

explanation.surface: A tune sung by a little girl during the afternoon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'performed by' is only a link; 'in' sets the girl's pet name within the afternoon's abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A sacred hymn, especially one from the biblical book of 150 such songs.

clue.text: School head to request quiet-total quiet

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a hush is complete silence

explanation.surface: A headteacher asks for silence, then complete silence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'School head' reads as the headteacher but gives only the first letter of School.
explanation.definitionFit: To tell someone to be silent, often with a finger to the lips.

clue.text: Chief means of support

definitions.meaning: a curved structure holding up a bridge or roof

explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means principal or main; as a noun it is a curved span bearing weight.

clue.text: The little blood-sucker may run away, one hears

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'The little blood-sucker may run away, one hears' for PLEA: the wordplay gives FLEA (a homophone of flee), not PLEA, so the answer or clue is misread.
annotationWithheld.clue: The little blood-sucker may run away, one hears

clue.text: I call out Miss Black's first name

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are knocked out of order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone shouts for a woman by the forename of Miss Black.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' signals an anagram of I CALL. CILLA Black was a popular British singer and TV presenter.
explanation.definitionFit: The singer and television host Cilla Black was known by this given name.

clue.text: Book for the big race?

definitions.meaning: a work of literature of lasting quality
one of the five major British flat horse races

explanation.surface: A betting form guide for a major horse race.
explanation.walkthrough: The five Classics are the top British flat races for three-year-olds, such as the Derby.
explanation.definitionFit: A great enduring novel is so called, as are the five most prestigious British horse races.

clue.text: A new role in flight control

indicators.note: new suggests the words that follow are given a fresh order of letters

explanation.surface: Someone takes on a fresh job in air-traffic control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' signals an anagram of ROLE IN, giving ILERON after A.
explanation.definitionFit: A hinged flap on an aircraft wing used to control roll is a primary flying control surface.

clue.text: Bays of victory

parts.note: bay leaves woven into a wreath crowned winners in ancient games

explanation.definitionFit: The bay tree's leaves, worn as a crown, symbolised triumph and honour.

clue.text: A short dress mother, to say the least

parts.note: a mini is a short skirt or dress
mum is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: Mum in a tiny dress is, putting it mildly, a surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: The smallest possible amount is what remains when nothing less is allowed.

clue.text: Resident is at home with his wife

parts.note: in means at home, as in staying in
a mate is a spouse or partner

explanation.surface: The man of the house is in with his spouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A person living in an institution, such as a prison or hospital, is one who dwells there.

clue.text: Ernest goes out and comes in

indicators.note: goes out suggests the name is disordered, its letters put in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Ernest leaves the room and then walks back in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes out' signals an anagram of ERNEST.
explanation.definitionFit: To go into a room or building is to step inside it.

clue.text: Doctor on morning rounds

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed below the other piece

parts.note: AM, ante meridiem, means morning
MO, medical officer, is a doctor

explanation.surface: A doctor visits patients on the ward in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rounds' suggests a doctor's ward rounds; it means bullets.
explanation.definitionFit: Rounds of shot or bullets are ammunition, of which this is the slang short form.

clue.text: New labs block

indicators.note: new suggests the letters of the word labs are put in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Newly built laboratories form a block of a building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' signals an anagram of LABS.
explanation.definitionFit: A thick flat piece of stone or concrete is a solid chunk of material.

clue.text: Turnover from two seasons, say

indicators.note: say means the words are spoken out loud and heard as another word

parts.note: summer is a season of the year, and salt seasons food

explanation.surface: A change from one season to another, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two seasons' suggests two times of year, but only summer is one; salt is a seasoning.
explanation.definitionFit: A head-over-heels flip of the body is a roll or turn over in the air.

clue.text: Women in retreat

parts.note: sounds like women fleeing, but refers to women who have withdrawn from the world to a religious house

explanation.definitionFit: Sisters of a religious order withdraw from ordinary life into a convent.

clue.text: China's sovereign race

parts.note: the crown stands for the sovereign or monarch
the Derby is a famous English horse race

explanation.surface: The Chinese ruler is racing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' suggests the country but means porcelain: Crown Derby is fine English porcelain from Derby.
explanation.definitionFit: A celebrated English porcelain made in Derby, so a kind of fine tableware.
